findings.reason: Verified in CPython's multiprocessing design that SpawnProcess derives from BaseProcess, not context.Process, so the isinstance check at line 254 is always False and kill() never runs on a hung flusher before a replacement is started on the same shards.

Confirmed in buffer.py that max_segments_per_shard = ceil(max_flush_segments / len(assigned_shards)) is computed per buffer, so per-process buffers with fewer shards raise both the total flush per cycle (up to P times) and the per-shard backpressure threshold, a real semantic shift in the option.

The shared client from redis.redis_clusters.get_binary is confirmed, so looping over buffers repeats the same INFO memory calls per submit, but this is a minor performance inefficiency rather than a correctness defect.
Confirmed that the test's monkeypatch of time.sleep makes the added time.sleep(0.1) a no-op, so the comment is misleading, but the test outcome is unaffected.

Confirmed that test_flusher_processes_limit only checks map counts and no test exercises multi-process restart or flushing across split shards, though this is a non-critical path gap capped at test-gap.
The docstring says one process per shard, but with the CLI default of 1 all shards share one process, so the docstring is slightly inaccurate, which is a documentation-only issue.

Verified that _create_process_for_shard has no callers and that the 'if not process' guard can never trigger since started Process and Thread objects are truthy, so both are dead code, a cleanup concern only.
Confirmed in the diff that wait_produce uses the tag key 'shards' while produce and segment_size_bytes use 'shard', an inconsistency in metric tagging that is a style/cleanup concern.
